# Dictionary generated by gradient-flow derivatives at fixed probes

New study, 2026-09-21. The user asks whether a dictionary generated from successive physical-time derivatives of the canonical middle-weight gradient is better aligned with learning than the existing polynomial core, and requests explicit terms using two fixed axis probes to avoid sample-count-dependent dictionary growth.

## Scope and contract

The original request was theory only; the later explicit authorization below adds a bounded empirical comparison. No maintained code/book change or promotion is authorized. Two hidden tanh layers, no biases, input dimension two, unhalved weighted probability mean square loss, physical mobilities `(n,1,n)`, canonical Gaussian hidden initialization, and zero limiting population readout. Finite-width identities using exactly zero readout are distinguished from the actual small random finite readout. The original proposed probe inputs are literal `e1,e2`; the input factor `1/sqrt(2)` is retained. The book's radius-sqrt(2) probes are a separate scaling and are identified explicitly when comparing dictionary formulas.

Derive the first three powers of time in the middle-weight velocity, retain moving residuals and both trained hidden blocks, and describe a label-independent hierarchy by extracting coefficients in symbolic probe labels. Fixed-probe dictionary size may depend on time-derivative order but not the later training sample count. Exact matching for arbitrary additional input directions is not presumed. No convergence of the infinite time series, autonomous closure theorem, or empirical superiority is claimed.

## Results and checks

- [DERIVATION.md](DERIVATION.md) gives the exact finite-order expansion on the continuous local population flow through cubic middle-weight velocity, including moving residuals, readout feedback and both trained hidden blocks. The equal-weight literal-axis expansion is `dot W2=(t-3 tau t^2/2+7 tau^2 t^3/6)D+t^3 F+o_HS(t^3)`. New adjoint and forward queries first enter this velocity at cubic order, or the weights at quartic order.
- [ALGEBRA_CHECK.md](ALGEBRA_CHECK.md) independently derives general weighted-input coefficients and verifies the symmetric specialization. [STRUCTURE_CHECK.md](STRUCTURE_CHECK.md) independently establishes the conditional-variance and fixed-input scope claims under the supplied Gaussian response rule. These are internal derivations/checks, not promotion reviews.
- The leading upper products are already degree-three polynomials in the old upper activations. Their reverse images retain strictly positive conditional variance given the old four lower core features. Therefore arbitrary polynomial enrichment of that fixed core cannot recover those fields; the full book hierarchy with added action words is not covered by that obstruction.
- A fixed-probe, fixed-order differentiation graph gives a sample-count-independent dictionary. It is exact for the corresponding finite-probe jets when the required intermediate fields and unbiased projections are retained, and is a proposal for approximation on other inputs. No superiority, all-order series convergence, finite-time closure convergence or blanket finite-dimensional impossibility is claimed.

The deterministic algebra oracle [jet_check.py](jet_check.py) implements truncated-series arithmetic on the full finite canonical vector field independently of the manual coefficient formulas. Four width-seven cases cover axes, correlated inputs with unequal weights, duplicate inputs, and zero labels. Each passed the predeclared absolute tolerance `2e-13`; the maximum observed discrepancy was `6.938893903907228e-18`. This is numerical verification of an exact algebra identity, not training or a population experiment. The symmetric population Gram simplification was checked analytically rather than inferred from a finite sample.

## Follow-up: indexing and counting the increment dictionary

The user requested indexing by powers in `W^(2)(t)` and counts at orders one and two. [ORDER_COUNTS.md](ORDER_COUNTS.md) fixes literal maximum Taylor power and distinguishes learned-increment factors from the larger full-closure feature lists. At zero population readout, the increment dictionary has lower/upper dimensions `(0,0)` through `t`, `(2,4)` through `t^2`, and the same `(2,4)` through `t^3` in the symmetric probe calculation. The latter gives six frozen functions and an unrestricted `4 by 2` middle matrix. A polynomial-support and label-family proof establishes minimality for these universal increment spans. Numbering the first two nonzero terms instead assigns both levels the same `(2,4)` dictionary. Scoped prompt-only agent `probe_order_count_check` independently checked the count distinctions; these are internal algebra results, not whole-network closure counts.

## Single-sample global-error theory for the same dictionary

The user's follow-up asks whether this derivative dictionary admits a global
error bound, beginning with one training sample. This is theoretical analysis
of the same specified closure; no training branch was reopened and no GPU
budget was consumed. Global means all physical times, and the main certificate
also covers passive inputs on the input ball/circle, beyond label fitting.

SINGLE_SAMPLE_GLOBAL_BOUND.md proves an all-time defect certificate for the
actual whole-middle, positive-ridge closure at exactly zero initial readout
(the population initialization), conditional only on nonzero initial upper
features in both models and the stated bounded-operator/Gaussian initial
integrability. For one sample, the readout obeys c_ss=T(s)c with T positive.
Convexity of ||c|| gives K>=||H0||², exponential label fitting and a bounded
residual clock. A tanh inverse-gate coordinate then gives a Lipschitz comparison
on that finite clock interval. Contracting scalar-clock comparison returns an
all-physical-time, whole-input-ball prediction bound C*epsilon_p.

The three explicitly defined epsilon_p terms measure omitted initialized
forward action, omitted initialized reverse action and filtered rank-one
update, all on the closure's own feature curve. No dense learned trajectory
is needed to define the certificate. The constants are explicit but can be
very large. This does NOT prove epsilon_p->0, a decay rate in p, or transfer
of the all-time theorem to the small nonzero readout of our executed finite
runs. The stronger population order-rate claim for the actual dictionary
remains open; local increment-jet containment does not close that gap.

SINGLE_SAMPLE_GLOBAL_CHECK.md independently checks the complete proof,
including population chain rules, existence, actual ridge lifting, constants,
clock contraction and passive-input control. Internal PASS for the exact
stated hypotheses; final checked proof SHA256
f16e11b19ebef54a1e7dfadf5e0a948e520353513835b892f4048ceaedd37c0d.
Root read the complete check and its limitations. SINGLE_SAMPLE_OBSTRUCTIONS.md
separately proves finite positive-ridge initialization mismatch and identifies
the missing seeds/probe/metric obligations without claiming a no-go theorem.

SINGLE_SAMPLE_ROUTE.md gives an independently derived residual-clock lemma
and a separate finite-width matched-jet route. A bounded complex tube and
three-circles propagation yield a geometric order tail at fixed finite width;
orthogonal update projection retaining W0 then has an all-time p-convergence
bound. This is explicitly a changed, background-preserving construction with
matched actual-sample derivatives. Whole compression retains initial and
ridge-mobility defects. Constants depend on width and can be impractically
large; no Gaussian-population order limit is inferred. Root read the full
route and checked its inequalities. Its degenerate fixed-probe witness applies
to exact finite jets, not the finite builder using ideal population moments.

No empirical claim or p7 result was changed, no maintained book/code/index
write occurred, and the remaining GPU allowance stays996.2095660865307.
The proved certificate is internally checked study material, not promoted.

## Attempt to prove population convergence in dictionary order

The user explicitly requested closing the remaining p->infinity convergence
gap. POPULATION_CONVERGENCE_ATTEMPT.md freezes that same-model target and
records three independent scoped routes plus the root's synthesis. No new
dictionary, training task, width limit, or experiment was substituted.

The attempt proves a weaker but definite limit theorem: any well-defined
nested L2 continuation of the actual raw lists with eta_p->0 has ridge
filters converging strongly to the orthogonal projections onto their closed
unions. No uniform Gram eigenvalue bound is needed. Its nonlinear population
closures consequently converge on every compact physical-time interval to
the projected limiting model with background P2 W2(0) P1 and middle update
(P2 Delta) tensor(P1 H1). If that limit has nonzero initial training energy,
convergence is uniform over all physical time and the passive input ball.
The positive-energy condition is proved for a sample at either fixed axis
probe, with exact zero population readout. This is convergence to the selected
closed-span dynamics; identification with the full dense population remains
open. No order rate or finite-width interchange was proved.
